brand.about: We have cut and stitched for other labels for seventeen years. The cloth, the tables, the pattern masters and the finishing line are ours; the name on the collar never was. This is the same floor, under our own name, with nobody in between.
brand.logoNote: The brand band at the top of every page. EMPTY means the drawn lockup in brand.js is used, which is what ships. To use a real logo: put the file in app/img/ and set this to its path relative to app/ -- "img/logo.svg". SVG is strongly preferred; a PNG needs to be about 3x the displayed height (so ~170px tall) or it will look soft on a phone. data.pl FAILS if this names a file that is not on disk, so a typo is a check failure and not a broken image a customer finds. A LEADING SLASH ALSO FAILS: a root-relative path works locally and breaks on GitHub Pages, which serves from a subpath. The band sets the height and leaves the width free, so any aspect ratio drops in without moving the page.
brand.name: Vastra Apparel
brand.tagline: Made on our own floor. Sold with nobody in between.

coupons.note: Exactly ONE of percent / flat per code -- data.pl fails on both or neither. minItems is measured on the ITEMS total BEFORE any discount, because a discount code must not be able to unlock itself. Matched case-insensitively with spaces stripped, since nobody types a code carefully. Set active:false to withdraw a code without losing the record of it.

gateway.note: SEE CLAUDE.md. While keyId is empty, card and net banking stay DISABLED WITH THE REASON ON THE CONTROL -- never hidden. A hidden option reads as a shop that does not take cards; a disabled one with its reason reads as a shop still setting up. data.pl FAILS if live is true while serverBase is empty: a gateway without a server cannot verify a payment, and flipping one boolean must not be able to make this site claim otherwise. It also FAILS on an rzp_test_ key with live true.

Hip.how: Around the fullest part of your hips, roughly 8 in below your waist, with your feet together.

Length.how: Measured on the garment, from the highest point of the shoulder straight down to the hem.

Shoulder.how: Measured on the garment, seam to seam across the back.

Sleeve.how: Measured on the garment, from the shoulder seam to the end of the sleeve.

To fit bust.how: Around the fullest part of your bust, keeping the tape level across your back and not pulled tight.

To fit chest.how: Around the fullest part of your chest, under the arms, keeping the tape level and not pulled tight.

Waist.how: Around your natural waist — the narrowest part, roughly level with your navel.

measureNotesNote: ⚠️ SOME COLUMNS ARE YOUR BODY AND SOME ARE THE GARMENT, and confusing the two is the single most common way a customer orders the wrong size. A 'To fit chest' of 40 means the shirt is cut to fit a 40 in CHEST; the garment itself measures more than that, because it needs ease to be wearable. A customer who measures a shirt they already own against a body column reads every size as too small and orders up. So every column declares `on`, the chart prints that next to the heading, and data.pl FAILS if a column in any chart has no note here or if a note is orphaned. Keyed by the column heading exactly as sizeCharts spells it -- rename a column and the check tells you immediately rather than the table quietly losing its guidance.

img/site/hero-floor.jpg.what: Home page, why it costs less

photosNote: Every photograph the site shows, keyed by its path: who took it, where it came from, and the exact crop fetched, so it can be fetched again at another size. data.pl FAILS if a photograph is shown with no entry here, if an entry names a file nothing shows, or if a file in app/img is shown by nothing. ⚠️ stock:true MEANS A STAND-IN -- a photograph of somebody else's garment, used under the Unsplash License until this shop's own are taken. data.pl FAILS if placeholder goes false while any stock photograph is still shown, because on a real shop a stand-in is a picture of a garment the customer will not receive. The About page draws its credits from this same list, so a credit cannot go missing when a photograph is added.
placeholderNote: WHILE THIS IS TRUE, data.pl FAILS. The brand name, the brand story, the year, every contact field and all three prices are INVENTED -- realistic, not real. The owner has not chosen a name yet. A phone number that does not dial and a GSTIN that is not yours are the worst things to ship by accident on a real business site, so this flag makes shipping them impossible rather than merely inadvisable. Set it to false only when every field in `contact` is real and the prices have been checked. data.pl then checks every contact field is non-empty -- including returnsAddr, which a shop selling to strangers must publish and a kirana delivering down the lane never needed. The Preview only bar at the top of every page is shown by this same flag, and goes when it does.

returns.note: ⚠️ SEVEN DAYS FROM DELIVERY, NOT FROM PLACEMENT. `from` is `delivery` and nothing may change that to `placed` without the owner saying so: a parcel that takes ten days to arrive would otherwise have its return window expire three days before it landed. This means `deliveredAt` MUST be stored the moment the status becomes `delivered`, and the window is counted from that stamp. ⚠️ `free: true` IS A COST, NOT A FEATURE -- for a manufacturer with no reverse logistics it can mean eating the courier both ways on a ₹700 kurti. NOT YET CONFIRMED WITH THE OWNER. Until it is, this number is a promise the app is making on their behalf.

shipping.note: DELIVERY IS FREE EVERYWHERE -- fee 0, freeOver 0. ⚠️ That makes the free-shipping threshold rule DORMANT, which is exactly how the same rule hid a real disagreement in kirana for months: its domain.js measured the threshold after the coupon and its money.pl measured it before, and both were invisible because both numbers were zero. money.pl here therefore pins the rule against a SYNTHETIC fee and threshold, so the check keeps testing the rule rather than testing zero. freeOver is measured on the ITEMS total, BEFORE any coupon: a discount code must not win free shipping a basket had not earned. deliveryDays is the five-to-ten-day promise, in ONE place, so changing it is an edit and not a code change -- and it is FROZEN INTO THE ORDER at placement, never recomputed on the tracking screen. basis `working` means Monday to Saturday, excluding Sunday.

men-shirt.fit: Relaxed fit. Measure around the fullest part of your chest, keeping the tape level. If you are between two sizes, take the larger.
men-shirt.label: Men's shirts

women-dress.fit: Relaxed through the body. Length is measured from the shoulder seam to the hem. If you are between two sizes, take the larger.
women-dress.label: Dresses

women-kurti.fit: Straight cut, not fitted. Length is measured from the shoulder seam to the hem. If you are between two sizes, take the larger.
women-kurti.label: Kurtis

sizeChartsNote: ⚠️ THE CHEAPEST RETURN PREVENTION THERE IS. Most clothing returns are fit, so this table is not decoration. Measurements are in inches, and EACH COLUMN DECLARES whether it is the body or the garment -- see measureNotes, which is where that is said and checked. One chart per garment type rather than per product, because a shirt in M is the same M across every shirt on this floor; repeating five rows on every product is how the numbers drift apart. A product names its chart with `sizeChart`, and data.pl FAILS if the chart is missing or does not carry a row for every size that product sells -- a size with no row renders a blank line in the table, which a customer reads as 'no measurement needed for XXL' rather than as a missing number. Row keys are the size ids from the catalogue, not the labels, so renaming a label never silently detaches the measurements from the size. `fit` is the one-line advice under the table; it is where the between-sizes rule goes, because that is the sentence people actually read. ⚠️ THESE NUMBERS ARE INVENTED, like the prices. They are a realistic Indian grading, not this manufacturer's own spec sheet. Get the real grading before anybody orders from it.

upi.note: A DELIBERATELY UNRESOLVABLE id. `example` is not a real UPI handle, so no payment app can find a payee and money physically cannot move. While demo is true the pay block wears a visible amber strip saying so. data.pl FAILS if demo is true and the handle after the @ is a real one (ybl, okaxis, paytm, ...), because a demo id on a live handle could send a customer's money to whoever owns it. To go live: put the real id in and set demo to false -- the strip disappears by itself.
